welcome_heatPumpQuestion: How does a heat pump work?
welcome_presetNoneReply: A heat pump moves heat instead of making it. A fluid absorbs warmth from the outside air, a compressor squeezes it so it gets hotter, and that heat is released inside your home. In summer the cycle can run in reverse to cool.
welcome_presetShortReply: It pulls warmth from the outside air and concentrates it with a compressor. Then it releases that heat indoors — like a fridge working in reverse.
welcome_presetNewInstruction: I’m not technical. Use everyday comparisons.
welcome_presetNewReply: Think of a fridge: it takes heat out of the inside and puffs it out the back. A heat pump does the same thing, but points the warm side at your living room — even cold winter air still has some warmth to borrow.
welcome_presetTeacherInstruction: I teach 12-year-olds in Lugano. Suggest a classroom activity.
welcome_presetTeacherReply: A heat pump borrows heat from outside air and moves it indoors. Classroom idea: have pupils feel the back of the school fridge, then ask where that warmth came from — it’s the same trick, run the other way.

Which datacenter runs a reply is chosen per request; each answer’s X-ray names it, and the same numbers apply throughout, so replies served elsewhere are rougher.

message_weakIntro: Where this system is systematically weak. We show these so you can weigh an answer rather than just take it — the opposite of a tool that hides its limits.
message_weakRecencyBody: It has a knowledge cutoff, so it can be out of date. When a question needs recent facts, Alpha searches the web and lists its sources; without sources, treat “latest” claims with care.
message_weakLookupBody: Open X-ray under an answer: it says whether Alpha looked anything up, and links each source it read so you can open it. An answer with nothing looked up is recalled from what the model learned, not quoted from a source. Recall can be confidently wrong; a citation is something you can check.
message_weakLanguageBody: Alpha’s models are strongest in English and widely-resourced languages. Quality and accuracy drop in lower-resourced languages — a known gap in the open stack, not a guarantee of equal quality everywhere.
message_weakPerspectiveBody: Its training data over-represents some countries, cultures, and viewpoints, so its “default” answer can quietly carry one perspective as if it were neutral. On contested or culturally specific questions, ask whose view it is giving you.
message_weakAdviceBody: It is not a substitute for a doctor, lawyer, financial adviser, or mental-health professional. For anything high-stakes, verify with a qualified human.
message_weakWrongBody: Different open models answer different messages. The model and its sources are named under each answer, so you can check them.
message_weakFooter: More on data, safety, and how to flag a wrong answer is on the {link} page.

contribute_evaluateYours: Help evaluate models in your language
contribute_evaluateBody: Benchmarks show whether a model understands a language, not whether its answers read naturally, get everyday tasks right or are safe. People who speak it can tell. Rate answers from Alpha’s models, without seeing which model wrote each one.
contribute_benchmarksTitle: Check how models do in your language
contribute_benchmarksBody: Auto picks a model for each message from scores that are still early estimates. Try messages in your language, see how every model ranks, and correct the scores you know are wrong.
contribute_feedbackBody: A language Alpha stumbles in, a tool you expected, a model you’d like to see — tell us, and it goes to the people building Alpha.
contribute_intro: Alpha is a potluck: every model, dataset and tool in it was brought by someone. The places it’s still weak — a language, a benchmark, a missing piece of the stack — are where your help counts most.
contribute_dataYours: Help improve data for your language
contribute_gapNotice: You wrote in {language}. None of Alpha’s models handle it dependably yet: the best manages about {percent}% on our early estimates.
contribute_dataBody: Models are weaker in some languages for several reasons: how they were trained, how they were tested, and how much text in the language they had to learn from. Data is one of those reasons, and it’s one you can help with. On {voice}, anyone can read sentences aloud or write new ones to build an open dataset in their language. What you add goes into open releases: you can ask to be left out of future ones, but not out of copies already downloaded or used for training. If your community already has data, the {org} lets it share that data on its own terms: who can use it, and for what.
contribute_dataLead: Pick your language, then choose one way to help.
contribute_dataPartners: Data goes to {voice} and the {org}, in a new tab. What you add joins open releases, and can’t be pulled from copies already downloaded.

routing_weightsHelp: Weights: how much each criterion counts when it fully applies. Only the ratios matter. For a message, each weight is scaled by how sure the classifier is that the criterion applies (the language detection, or a skill it needs), then they’re shared out to 100%. A skill scored in the benchmark table adds its own row here.

run_fact_languages: No single model is best in every language. Open models from Switzerland, Spain, Singapore, Poland and beyond each bring languages of their own.
run_fact_data: Open data comes from many hands: recorded voices, shared datasets, and open knowledge like Wikipedia and OpenAlex.
run_fact_compute: Open models are trained on public supercomputers like CSCS and BSC, then run by many different hosts.
run_fact_together: {count} parts of Alpha's open stack are still open invitations. Bring one.

run_why_data: Open models are only as good as the open data they learn from.
run_why_evals: Someone has to check the answers, in every language.
run_why_models: Which open model or tool should Alpha add next? You help decide.
run_why_compute: Open models run on public supercomputers and independent clouds alike. See where the open stack is strong, and where it has gaps.
run_why_none: Every piece of open source AI is brought by someone.
